answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with slow decay: an agent must lock a bond before it can transact, and each verified task adds reputation that compounds over time. A sybil swarm faces a gale of upfront costs — thousands of bonds with no history — while honest agents climb out of the canyon of cold start through real work. Fake identities cannot fake time: their reputation stays near zero, and any coordinated burst looks like a spiral of identical low-value activity that anomaly scoring flags and throttles before it drains the treasury.
